featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a true food lover, Noor Mohammadi Hotel is nothing short of heaven. I finally got to try their legendary Nalli Nihari, and honestly… it lives up to every bit of the hype.

The nihari was rich, slow-cooked to perfection, with the marrow melting into the gravy, bursting with deep, soulful flavors. Every spoon felt warm, comforting, and indulgent — the kind of dish that makes you pause and appreciate good food.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, the meal ended with their Rabdi. Thick, creamy, and perfectly balanced in sweetness, it was the ideal dessert to round off such a hearty feast. You can actually taste the patience and tradition in every bite.
No fancy plating, no unnecessary drama — just authentic, old-school flavors that hit straight to the heart. Noor Mohammadi doesn’t just serve food; it serves heritage on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Kadir
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place truly gave me a heartwarming experience and the kind of food that reminds you what real, honest cooking tastes like. It’s amazing to know that this restaurant has been around for over 102 years, carrying forward a legacy of authentic flavors and consistent quality. You can really feel that heritage in every dish they serve.

The food was absolutely delicious and clearly made with care and good-quality ingredients. I loved how every bite had that traditional touch — nothing fancy, just pure, flavorful food made right. My personal favorites were the Mutton Sanju Baba and the Haleem. The mutton was soft, juicy, and full of flavor, while the haleem was rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced — the kind that instantly makes you smile after the first spoonful.

The ambiance adds to the experience — simple, calm, and full of character. It feels like a place where stories have been shared for generations. The staff was really friendly and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying our food.

Overall, I’d say this isn’t just a restaurant it’s a part of culinary history. If you love traditional, soulful food that warms both your heart and your stomach, this place is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Noor Mohammadi Hotel and it was a truly memorable experience for anyone who loves authentic Mughlai food. This place is quite iconic and well-known for its rich, flavorful dishes.

The highlight, of course, is their legendary chicken dishes—especially the Chicken Sanju Baba, which is packed with bold spices and has a rich, indulgent taste. The food overall is delicious, with generous portions and that proper old-school Mumbai Mughlai flavor.

The ambience is simple and no-frills, but that’s part of its charm. It’s more about the food than the setting. The place is usually quite crowded, and you might have to wait a bit for a table, especially during peak hours.

Service is quick considering the rush, though it can feel a bit hectic at times. Hygiene and seating are decent but not luxurious, so it’s best to go in with the right expectations.

Overall, Noor Mohammadi is a must-visit if you’re looking to enjoy authentic, hearty Mughlai cuisine in Mumbai. It’s not about fine dining, but about great taste and a truly local food experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

On reminding the new staff (as old staff had vanished), they punched in repeat item in our bill, even though delivery happened only once! Due to their poor service I had to pay for an extra Juice! Not a nice experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Highly Disappointing Maharashtrian Food
Overall Rating: 3/10 (Based primarily on food Taste and facilities)
My recent visit to Vinay in Girgaon was a profound disappointment, particularly for anyone seeking authentic, high-quality Maharashtrian snacks. The experience was marred by poor execution of core dishes and subpar facilities, resulting in one of the worst quick-service dining experiences I've had in a while.
The Food Verdict
The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Stepping into DELHI RASOI is an exercise in managing expectations. If you're looking for sprawling dining halls, endless menu pages, or a spot for a large, rowdy gathering, this isn't it. But if you're a vegetarian seeking a perfectly executed, intensely flavorful meal that bypasses quantity for sheer quality, you absolutely must find this little 💎 GEM
​The space is small and intimate. The tables are close, the movement is restricted, and during peak hours, the atmosphere can feel more bustling. It has a focused, cozy, and slightly chaotic energy that somehow feels authentic—you know the kitchen is working hard just feet away.
​The starter and main course sections are intentionally limited. This might initially feel restrictive, but it quickly becomes RASOI's superpower. Instead of spreading its focus on Quantity, Rasoi concentrates on Quality, perfecting a handful of dishes.
The flavor is where this restaurant shines, brilliantly exceeding its humble surroundings. We tried the "Cheese Corn Ball, Paneer Chilli, Mushroom Chilli, Cheese Paratha" to start, and they were crispy on the outside, tender inside, and packed with a fresh, vibrant kick that felt utterly homemade. For the main, "Paneer Lababdar, Baigaan Bharta, Tadka Kadi Pakoda with Butter & Ghee Phulkas" was a revelation—rich, creamy, and complex, clearly cooked with ingredients and balanced spices. Every dish we sampled was bursting with deep, memorable flavor, proving that the kitchen staff are true masters of their craft.
​The verdict:
DELHI RASOI is the ideal spot for a quick, exceptionally tasty lunch or an intimate dinner where the focus is solely on the plate. Come for the fantastic food, not the fancy décor or extensive options. Just be prepared to wait a little, if you arrive at a busy time, and know that every bite is worth the WAIT.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Atul Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went for a Sunday brunch, and the restaurant manages to strike a nice balance between being busy and still feeling comfortable. The ambience is simple yet pleasant, with ample seating available in both AC and non-AC sections. Despite the steady crowd, the space feels organized and welcoming.

Since it was a Sunday, there was a queue when I arrived, and the waiting time was around 25 to 30 minutes before getting seated. However, the seating turnover is quite efficient, and once seated the service moves quickly. The overall setup works well for a place that sees such heavy footfall.

The Food
Rava Masala Dosa (Ghee): This was exactly what you would expect from a good South Indian restaurant, earning 3.8 to 4 out of 5. The dosa had the right texture and flavor profile.

Ulundu Dosa: Made primarily with urad dal, this dosa had a very distinct flavor. While it may appeal to those who enjoy that strong taste, it personally didn’t work for me as much, which places it at 2.5 out of 5.

Davangere Benne Dosa (with Cheese): This was something different from the usual dosa offerings. The flavor was again quite distinct, but it still carried an interesting richness and character. Overall, it lands at about 3 out of 5.

Bisibele Bath: This was a pleasant addition to the meal, earning 3.5 out of 5. The flavor was quite good, with the comforting, mildly spiced profile you expect from a well-made bisibele bath. However, the portion size felt noticeably small, which slightly took away from the overall experience. Taste-wise it delivered, but a larger serving would have made it far more satisfying.

Sides
Kothimbir Vadi: A tasty accompaniment that scored 3.5 out of 5. The flavor was enjoyable, though the preparation felt slightly oily.

Sabudana Vada: This was one of the highlights among the sides, easily earning 4.5 out of 5. The texture and flavor worked very well, making it a standout snack.

Beverage
Filter Coffee: Surprisingly, the coffee felt fairly average compared to the rest of the meal. It was decent but not particularly memorable, coming in at 3 out of 5.

Dessert
Mysore Pak: This was easily the best part of the entire meal. Rich, indulgent, and incredibly satisfying, it completely stole the show. If ratings allowed it, this would easily be a 10 out of 5.

Sambar & Chutney
Considering Ramashraya’s reputation, both the sambar and coconut chutney felt fairly average. They complemented the dishes but did not particularly stand out.

Overall Verdict
For a total bill of around ₹550, Ramashraya offers a solid dining experience with a wide variety of traditional South Indian options. While some dishes had very distinct flavor profiles that may not appeal to everyone, items like the Sabudana Vada and especially the Mysore Pak make the visit worthwhile. If you do visit, make sure you don’t leave without trying the Mysore Pak—it’s easily the highlight of the meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Ram Ashraya near charni road station, and it turned out to be an amazing experience for South Indian food lovers. This place is quite popular in Matunga and has a long-standing reputation for serving authentic and delicious dishes.
The restaurant has a simple, old-school vibe, but that’s part of its charm. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient. It is located at a walkable distance from charni road station, which makes it very convenient to visit.
We tried some of their signature dishes, including ghee podi masala dosa, benne dosa, and sweet Mysore pak. Each dish was packed with flavor and tasted absolutely delicious. The dosas were perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, with generous use of ghee that enhanced the overall taste. The podi masala added a spicy and aromatic touch, making it a must-try item.
The Mysore pak was another highlight—soft, rich, and perfectly sweet, making it a great way to end the meal. One of the best things about this place is that the food is budget-friendly despite its high quality, which makes it a favorite among students and locals.
Overall, Ram Ashraya is a must-visit spot if you’re craving authentic South Indian food in Mumbai. Whether you’re going for breakfast or a quick meal, this place won’t disappoint. Highly recommended for anyone looking for tasty, affordable, and satisfying South Indian dishes!
